@graph.description:
Replication of nav2's wait-behavior system test
(nav2_system_tests/src/behaviors/wait, main). Where upstream drives the /wait
action with a C++ tester (wait_behavior_tester.cpp) against a tb3 Gazebo world,
this campaign runs the full nav2 stack (files/nav2_stack.launch.py, the same
hexagon world as the sibling error_codes and system_failure campaigns) and drives
/wait with the generic action_call primitive.

MEANING OF A CELL: one configuration is one upstream wait parameterization
(nav2_system_tests.csv lines 23-26, test case `test_wait_behavior`). The wait behavior
SUCCEEDS after its configured duration, so every ported cell carries
expect_success: true and action_call returns SUCCESS -- the same assertion
wait_behavior_tester.cpp's behaviorTest() makes. The analysis additionally verifies
the upstream `elapsed >= wait_time` assertion from the recorded /wait/_action
timestamps (not expressible in the scenario; see wait_behavior.osc header).

PORTED CASE -> DURATION:
- Wait 1 (CSV line 23) -> 1.0 s
- Wait 2 (CSV line 24) -> 2.0 s
- Wait 5 (CSV line 25) -> 5.0 s

NOT PORTED: Wait 10 + cancel (CSV line 26). behaviorTestCancel() sends a /wait goal
then async_cancel_all_goals and asserts the goal was canceled; a mid-run cancel
cannot be sequenced in this scenario framework (action_call has no cancel entry
point -- RosActionCall.shutdown() cancels only at scenario teardown). Recorded,
not faked, in readme.md.

UPSTREAM ODDITY worth recording: upstream CMakeLists.txt sets
BT_NAVIGATOR_XML=navigate_to_pose_w_replanning_and_behavior.xml, a file that exists
neither in the navigation2 source tree nor in the installed nav2_bt_navigator share
directory (verified in the robovast image). It is immaterial here -- /wait is a
behavior-server action, not a BT node -- but the CSV row's BT column therefore names
a file that cannot be loaded.
